network.overall_strategy: Mechanistically, the network is anchored on the Shen-Yang-Miller-Oro sequence, the only experimentally resolved histidine route: formaldehyde is carried forward to erythrose, erythrose plus formamidine gives imidazole-4-acetaldehyde or the observed coproduct reservoirs imidazole-4-glycol and imidazole-4-ethanol, and the aldehyde then undergoes Strecker cyanation and hydrolysis to histidine. Because erythrose availability and formamidine persistence are major criticisms, the upstream formaldehyde-to-erythrose step and the ethanol-to-aldehyde oxidation are flagged as speculative or low-confidence feeders. To remain literature-complete without overstating mechanism, three additional aggregate source terms are included for electrical discharge, CO/H2/NH3 heterogeneous catalysis, and UV/EUV PAH-ice photochemistry. No vent-specific hydrothermal sequence is invented because the supplied literature does not demonstrate one and amino acids are thermally fragile at the hottest vent conditions. Several listed pathways are late-stage subroutes through experimentally observed intermediates so that 10 pathways can be given without fabricating unsupported chemistry.

reactions.name: Formose-derived erythrose formation

conditions.other: Wet-dry concentration in alkaline surface pools; represented as the balanced net tetramerization 4 CH2O -> C4H8O4.

reactions.mechanism: Base-enabled formose/aldol sequence giving a tetrose fraction that includes erythrose.
reactions.reasoning: Included as a speculative feeder to the Shen network because formaldehyde-to-tetrose chemistry is the chemically natural upstream source of erythrose, which Shen et al. (1987) treated as a plausible prebiotic feedstock, while Vazquez-Salazar et al. (2018) emphasized that erythrose is a minor and unstable formose product. No histidine paper in the supplied set directly demonstrated this step, so it is marked speculative.

reactions.name: Erythrose-formamidine cyclocondensation to imidazole-4-acetaldehyde

conditions.other: Warm concentrated aqueous solution near pH 6; balanced net is erythrose + formamidine -> imidazole-4-acetaldehyde + 3 H2O.

reactions.mechanism: Amadori-like condensation, rearrangement, ring closure, and dehydration to the imidazole aldehyde.
reactions.reasoning: This is the best-supported histidine-specific precursor step in the literature: Shen et al. (1987) heated about 0.03 M erythrose with about 0.03 M formamidine at about pH 6 and 80 C and identified imidazole-4-acetaldehyde. The chemistry is strong even though the geochemical availability of both precursors remains contested (Shen et al., 1987; Vazquez-Salazar et al., 2018).

reactions.name: Erythrose-formamidine cyclocondensation to imidazole-4-glycol

conditions.other: Warm concentrated aqueous solution near pH 6; balanced net is erythrose + formamidine -> imidazole-4-glycol + 2 H2O.

reactions.mechanism: Alternative condensation/rearrangement branch that preserves a more reduced, hydrated side chain.
reactions.reasoning: Shen et al. (1987) also detected imidazole-4-glycol as a major coproduct from erythrose and formamidine, so this is an experimentally observed alternative branch rather than an invented intermediate. Its later conversion to histidine is less directly demonstrated than the aldehyde branch (Shen et al., 1987).

reactions.name: Imidazole-4-glycol dehydration to imidazole-4-acetaldehyde

conditions.other: Warm aqueous aging with mildly acidic intervals; balanced net is C5H8N2O2 -> C5H6N2O + H2O.

reactions.mechanism: Dehydrative collapse of the glycol reservoir to the validated aldehyde precursor.
reactions.reasoning: Shen et al. (1987) discussed imidazole-4-glycol as a plausible aldehyde reservoir, and dehydration to imidazole-4-acetaldehyde is chemically straightforward. The specific prebiotic dehydration step was not isolated in the supplied papers, so this edge is semi-speculative and is included to represent the observed coproduct reservoir (Shen et al., 1987; Vazquez-Salazar et al., 2018).

reactions.name: Erythrose-formaldehyde-ammonia condensation to imidazole-4-ethanol

conditions.other: Warm aqueous solution near pH 6.6; ammonium in the experiments is represented here by net NH3 stoichiometry, with the balanced net erythrose + formaldehyde + 2 NH3 -> imidazole-4-ethanol + 4 H2O.

reactions.mechanism: Carbonyl-ammonia condensation giving a reduced imidazole side chain alcohol instead of the aldehyde.
reactions.reasoning: Shen et al. (1987) obtained imidazole-4-ethanol from erythrose + formaldehyde + ammonium chemistry at about pH 6.6 and 80 C. This branch is experimentally observed, but it is not by itself a completed histidine synthesis; it is included as an alternative precursor reservoir rather than as a strongly validated route to the target (Shen et al., 1987).

reactions.name: Mineral-assisted dehydrogenation of imidazole-4-ethanol

conditions.other: Hot mineral films or low-water interfaces; balanced as alcohol dehydrogenation C5H8N2O -> C5H6N2O + H2.

reactions.mechanism: Mineral-assisted alcohol dehydrogenation/oxidation to the imidazole aldehyde.
reactions.reasoning: This oxidation/dehydrogenation is not demonstrated in the supplied histidine papers and should be treated as speculative. It is included only because Shen et al. (1987) identified imidazole-4-ethanol as a real coproduct and noted that conversion to the aldehyde would be needed for closure, while Vazquez-Salazar et al. (2018) highlighted that the redox step remains unresolved.

reactions.name: Strecker addition on imidazole-4-acetaldehyde

conditions.other: HCN- and NH3-bearing aqueous solution; balanced net is imidazole-4-acetaldehyde + NH3 + HCN -> histidine aminonitrile + H2O.

reactions.mechanism: Imine/iminium formation followed by cyanide capture to give the alpha-aminonitrile.
reactions.reasoning: This is the conventional Strecker capture of the validated imidazole aldehyde. Shen et al. (1990) experimentally closed the route by adding HCN and ammonia to the imidazole-precursor mixture, and the corresponding alpha-aminonitrile is the standard mechanistic intermediate for that chemistry (Shen et al., 1990).

reactions.name: Hydrolysis of histidine aminonitrile to histidine

conditions.other: Prolonged aqueous aging or geothermal cycling; balanced net consumes 2 H2O per aminonitrile and liberates NH3.

reactions.mechanism: Nitrile hydrolysis converts the alpha-aminonitrile into the amino acid carboxyl group.
reactions.reasoning: Hydrolysis of the alpha-aminonitrile to histidine is the conservative interpretation of the second half of the Shen synthesis. Histidine itself was identified by multiple chromatographic and mass-spectrometric methods in Shen et al. (1990), making this the most mechanistically secure completion step.

reactions.name: One-pot Shen-Oro histidine synthesis net step

conditions.other: Balanced net edge: erythrose + formamidine + HCN -> histidine + 2 H2O. NH3 is omitted because it is consumed in the Strecker stage but regenerated during aminonitrile hydrolysis.

reactions.mechanism: Aggregate two-stage sequence combining imidazole construction with Strecker closure and hydrolysis.
reactions.reasoning: This is a balanced aggregate representation of the experimentally closed Shen-Oro sequence, not an elementary step: erythrose + formamidine was first heated to generate imidazole intermediates, then HCN/ammonia was added to obtain histidine in 3.5% yield relative to erythrose (Shen et al., 1990). It is included because the paper demonstrated histidine formation without isolating the aldehyde intermediate.

reactions.name: Electrical-discharge histidine source term

conditions.temperature: 300-350 K bulk liquid; plasma microzones much hotter
conditions.other: Surface label used as an atmospheric discharge over water proxy. Net balance shown as 6 CH4 + 3 NH3 + 2 H2O -> histidine + 14 H2; H2 or N2 present in some experiments are treated as atmosphere components rather than required net inputs.

reactions.mechanism: Aggregate endpoint-only discharge chemistry involving gas-phase radicals, HCN/carbonyl generation, and secondary aqueous reactions.
reactions.reasoning: Histidine was reported from reduced-gas discharge chemistry, with Jiang et al. (2014) stating that all non-sulfur protein amino acids except glutamate were formed after seven days, and Criado-Reyes et al. (2021) later reported quantified histidine from CH4/NH3/N2/H2O discharges. Because neither study established a histidine-specific intermediate sequence and the 2021 assignment is less secure than the Shen route, this balanced edge is encoded only as an empirical source term (Jiang et al., 2014; Criado-Reyes et al., 2021).

reactions.name: Fischer-Tropsch-type catalytic histidine source term

conditions.other: Hydrothermal label here denotes hot catalytic mineral-surface chemistry rather than a demonstrated vent-wall sequence. Balanced net is 6 CO + 4 H2 + 3 NH3 -> histidine + 4 H2O.

reactions.mechanism: Aggregate high-temperature heterogeneous surface chemistry involving reduction, C-C bond formation, and nitrogen incorporation.
reactions.reasoning: Yoshino et al. (1971) reported histidine among amino acids formed from CO/H2/NH3 over Ni, alumina, or clay, and Hayatsu et al. (1971) reinforced the claim with deuterated feedstocks and mass spectrometry to address contamination. The mechanism and histidine-specific yield remained unresolved, and the high laboratory temperatures are not direct proof of a vent-safe accumulation route, so this is kept as a coarse-grained catalytic source term (Yoshino et al., 1971; Hayatsu et al., 1971; Ito et al., 2006).

reactions.name: UV-EUV PAH-ice histidine source term

conditions.temperature: 15 K irradiation, then warming and hydrolysis
conditions.other: Surface label is a schema proxy for exogenous irradiated ice delivered to a planetary surface. Based on a 1:1:1 naphthalene:H2O:NH3 ice; CO and H2 are bookkeeping coproducts included to balance the aggregate source term.

reactions.mechanism: Aggregate photochemical radical chemistry in PAH-rich ice followed by release of histidine or histidine-yielding precursors during hydrolysis.
reactions.reasoning: Chen et al. (2008) detected histidine after UV/EUV irradiation of a 1:1:1 naphthalene:H2O:NH3 ice followed by strong-acid hydrolysis. Because the ice ratios were deliberately NH3- and PAH-rich, the quantum yield was very low, and hydrolysis may have released histidine from acid-labile precursors rather than from free histidine formed in the ice, this edge is encoded as an aggregate photochemical/hydrolytic source term rather than an elementary reaction (Chen et al., 2008).

pathways.name: Full Shen aldehyde route from formaldehyde-derived erythrose
pathways.description: Speculative formaldehyde-to-erythrose feeding into the experimentally validated erythrose plus formamidine aldehyde branch, followed by Strecker closure.

pathways.name: Late-stage Shen aldehyde route from accumulated erythrose
pathways.description: Starts from pre-concentrated erythrose and uses the best-supported precursor step to imidazole-4-acetaldehyde before Strecker conversion to histidine.

pathways.name: Full glycol-reservoir route from formaldehyde-derived erythrose
pathways.description: A longer branch in which erythrose and formamidine first give the observed coproduct imidazole-4-glycol, which then collapses to the validated aldehyde precursor before Strecker closure.

pathways.name: Erythrose-to-histidine via the glycol reservoir
pathways.description: Begins after erythrose has accumulated and follows the experimentally observed imidazole-4-glycol branch into the semi-speculative dehydration step and then the validated Strecker sequence.

pathways.name: Formaldehyde-ammonia alcohol branch
pathways.description: Uses the observed erythrose plus formaldehyde plus ammonium branch to imidazole-4-ethanol, then a speculative mineral-assisted oxidation to the aldehyde, followed by Strecker closure.

pathways.name: Direct Strecker completion from imidazole-4-acetaldehyde
pathways.description: Late-stage closure from the validated imidazole aldehyde precursor through histidine aminonitrile to histidine.

pathways.name: Net Shen-Oro one-pot route
pathways.description: Aggregate representation of the experimentally closed two-stage erythrose plus formamidine plus HCN synthesis, entered here as a balanced net route from formaldehyde-derived erythrose.

pathways.name: Electrical-discharge endpoint route
pathways.description: Endpoint-only lightning or plasma route from reduced gases over water; histidine is reported experimentally but the molecular pathway remains unresolved.

pathways.name: Catalytic CO-H2-NH3 route
pathways.description: Historical Fischer-Tropsch-type mineral-surface source term from CO, H2, and NH3 at elevated temperature; histidine is reported but no target-specific mechanism is known.

pathways.name: PAH-ice photochemical route
pathways.description: Exogenous UV/EUV-processed naphthalene-rich ice residue that yields histidine on hydrolysis after warming and delivery; interpreted as an endpoint source term rather than a resolved mechanism.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Once erythrose is available, this is a chemically strong route and it aligns well with the Shen 1987/1990 sequence. Confidence is limited mainly by rxn_001, because uncontrolled formose chemistry gives erythrose only as a minor and unstable product, and the network does not specify how that feeder is staged or concentrated.
suggestions: Replace rxn_001 with an explicitly staged formose/concentration module or a more specific erythrose-generating feeder.
Specify aqueous, warm, mildly acidic conditions for rxn_002, rxn_007, and rxn_008 and explain transfer from the erythrose-forming stage.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: This is the best-supported full route in the network. Erythrose plus formamidine to imidazole-4-acetaldehyde, followed by Strecker cyanation and aminonitrile hydrolysis, matches the mechanistically resolved Shen literature; the main remaining weakness is geochemical availability and persistence of erythrose and formamidine rather than the core reaction chemistry itself.
suggestions: Annotate rxn_002, rxn_007, and rxn_008 with the Shen conditions, roughly 80 C, pH about 6, aqueous heating.
State explicitly that erythrose accumulation and formamidine hydrolysis are the key geochemical uncertainties.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: This is a reasonable variant because imidazole-4-glycol is an experimentally observed coproduct and could serve as a reservoir. The weak points are the speculative erythrose feeder in rxn_001 and the fact that rxn_004 is plausible but not an equally well closed prebiotic conversion under the supplied conditions.
suggestions: Provide literature support or explicit conditions for acid-catalyzed conversion of imidazole-4-glycol to the aldehyde.
Represent erythrose formation as a staged feeder rather than a single direct formaldehyde-to-erythrose edge.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: This is a coherent late-stage reservoir route if imidazole-4-glycol accumulates. Confidence is moderate-good, but the glycol to aldehyde handoff still needs stronger experimental closure under a defined prebiotic aqueous setting.
suggestions: Add direct evidence or a tighter literature justification for rxn_004 under prebiotic aqueous conditions.
Clarify that this pathway depends on prior accumulation of imidazole-4-glycol rather than demonstrating a fully closed source-to-target sequence.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: The alcohol branch is literature-grounded up to imidazole-4-ethanol in the Shen erythrose plus formaldehyde plus ammonium system, but it is not experimentally closed to histidine. rxn_006 is the major weakness: a realistic prebiotic oxidation or dehydrogenation system is not demonstrated here and no specific catalyst or oxidant is supplied.
suggestions: Replace rxn_006 with a justified oxidant or catalyst system, or mark it explicitly as hypothetical.
Keep this branch ranked below the validated aldehyde route unless direct prebiotic closure to the aldehyde is shown.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: This is the most chemically secure subroute in the network. From imidazole-4-acetaldehyde onward, the Strecker and aminonitrile hydrolysis logic is standard and well aligned with the Shen closure step, though this pathway does not address how the imidazole aldehyde is supplied.
suggestions: Mark P6 clearly as a late-stage subroute rather than a complete synthesis from simple feedstocks.
Add explicit hydrolysis stoichiometry and conditions for rxn_008.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: The one-pot histidine observation is literature-backed, but the compressed net representation is too loose. rxn_009 omits NH3 even though the Shen 1990 closure uses ammonia in the Strecker stage, so the edge should be treated as an empirical aggregate rather than a faithful mechanistic net reaction.
suggestions: Rewrite rxn_009 to include NH3 or explicitly label it as an empirical aggregate of the Shen 1990 mixture.
Avoid presenting the compressed net edge as mechanistically equivalent to the resolved aldehyde plus Strecker sequence.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: This is acceptable only as a coarse empirical source term, because histidine has been reported in spark-discharge experiments such as Jiang 2014 and Criado-Reyes 2021. It is not a mechanistically resolved pathway, and the Surface label omits the actual discharge atmosphere, aqueous interface, and energy input.
suggestions: Relabel the environment as electrical-discharge atmosphere or atmosphere-water interface and include the energy source explicitly.
Keep rxn_010 as an empirical source edge unless target-specific intermediates are established experimentally.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Histidine production from CO, H2, and NH3 over catalysts is historically supported by the 1971 Yoshino, Hayatsu, and Anders studies, but this network represents it poorly. The reaction is heterogeneous catalytic surface chemistry, not a validated hydrothermal histidine pathway, so environmental consistency is weak.
suggestions: Relabel rxn_011 as heterogeneous catalytic surface chemistry with Ni, alumina, or clay and appropriate temperature, not hydrothermal vent chemistry.
Treat the edge as endpoint-only evidence rather than a resolved histidine-specific mechanism.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: This is reasonable only as an empirical source term. Chen 2008 detected histidine after UV or EUV irradiation of PAH, H2O, and NH3 ice followed by acid hydrolysis, so the current edge overstates the result as direct single-step free-histidine formation on a generic surface.
suggestions: Relabel rxn_012 as UV or EUV irradiation of PAH, H2O, and NH3 ice at about 15 K with post-hydrolysis analysis.
State clearly that the measured histidine may arise from acid-labile precursors rather than free histidine already present in the irradiated ice.

evaluation.network_feedback: The network is connected, uses molecule IDs consistently, and has no mass or charge conservation failures under the supplied RDKit balance check. Literature alignment is strongest for the Shen-Yang-Miller-Oro core, and that part of the network is represented well: rxn_002, rxn_007, and rxn_008 are the best supported chemistry and make P2 the strongest pathway. The main weaknesses are environmental underspecification and several coarse or speculative edges: rxn_001 is only a low-selectivity erythrose feeder; rxn_004 is plausible but not equally well closed experimentally; rxn_006 is a speculative alcohol-to-aldehyde step; rxn_009 over-compresses the Shen 1990 one-pot experiment and should include NH3 or be labeled as an empirical aggregate; rxn_010 through rxn_012 are endpoint source terms rather than mechanistic single reactions; rxn_011 is misassigned as Hydrothermal rather than heterogeneous catalytic surface chemistry; and rxn_012 conflates ice photolysis with hydrolysis-released histidine. The repeated use of Biochemical as an environment label also lowers environmental consistency because it is not a geochemical setting. Add explicit stoichiometric coefficients to the reactions that are only balanceable with inferred coefficients, and provide temperature, pH, catalysts, and energy sources per environment. Overall this is a literature-aware and chemically plausible network in part, but it is not approved at the network level.
